p: בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה מח, ד): רַבִּי יִצְחָק פָּתַח: "מִזְבַּח אֲדָמָה תַּעֲשֶׂה לִּי וְגוֹמֵר בְּכָל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ" (שְׁמוֹת כ, כא

) – In Midrash Rabbah (Parashah 48:4): Rabbi Yitzchak opened his discourse: "'An altar of earth you shall make unto Me... in every place where I cause My name to be mentioned I will come unto you and bless you' (Exodus 20:21) –
מָה אִם זֶה שֶׁבָּנָה מִזְבֵּחַ לִשְׁמִי הֲרֵינִי נִגְלֶה עָלָיו וּמְבָרְכוֹ, אַבְרָהָם שֶׁמָּל עַצְמוֹ לִשְׁמִי עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה (שֶׁאֶתְגַּלֶּה עָלָיו, דִּכְתִיב: וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו ה
'). if regarding one who merely builds an altar of earth for My Name, behold, I am revealed to him and bless him, then regarding Abraham who circumcised his own flesh for My Name, how much more so!"
יֵשׁ לְהָבִין, הֵיכָן נִזְכַּר כָּאן שֶׁבֵּרַךְ לְאַבְרָהָם
? We must understand: where is there any mention here at the beginning of Vayera that God blessed Abraham?
בִּשְׁלָמָא שָׁם בַּמִּזְבֵּחַ כְּתִיב: "אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ", מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּאַבְרָהָם לֹא נִזְכַּר כָּאן רַק שֶׁנִּגְלָה עָלָיו ("וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו ה'") וְלֹא הוּזְכַּר בְּרָכָה

! Granted, there regarding the altar it is explicitly written, "I will come unto you and bless you"; whereas here regarding Abraham it states only that He appeared to him ("And Hashem appeared to him"), without mentioning any blessing!

גַּם מַה שֶּׁאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה מח, ה): "וְשׁוֹר וָאַיִל לִשְׁלָמִים לִזְבֹּחַ לִפְנֵי ה'... מָה אִם זֶה שֶׁהִקְרִיב שׁוֹר וָאַיִל לִשְׁמִי הֲרֵינִי נִגְלֶה עָלָיו וּמְבָרְכוֹ וְכוּלֵי

", Furthermore, regarding what Rabbi Levi says immediately afterward in Midrash Rabbah (48:5) on the verse "And an ox and a ram for peace-offerings, to sacrifice before Hashem... for today Hashem appears to you" (Leviticus 9:4): "If regarding one who offered an ox and a ram for My Name, behold, I am revealed to him and bless him, Abraham who circumcised himself for My Name, how much more so!"—
יֵשׁ לְהָבִין, דְּהָא גַּם שָׁם לֹא הוּזְכַּר בְּרָכָה, וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב אַחַר כָּךְ "וַיֵּצְאוּ וַיְבָרֲכוּ אֶת הָעָם" (וַיִּקְרָא ט, כג) רָחוֹק מִפָּסוּק "וְשׁוֹר וָאַיִל

"! this too requires explanation, for in that verse (Leviticus 9:4) no blessing is mentioned either, and what is written much later at the end of the chapter, "And Moses and Aaron went out and blessed the people" (Leviticus 9:23), is far removed from the verse "And an ox and a ram"!

p: אַךְ הָעִנְיָן, דְּעִיקַּר בְּרָכָה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
, However, the explanation is that the essential blessing of Hashem, blessed be He, consists of the illumination and expansion of words of Torah,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ סֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר (סִימָן ג): "וּמְנָלַן דְּאִיקְרֵי תּוֹרָה בְּרָכָה? דִּכְתִיב: וּמָלֵא בִּרְכַּת ה' יָם וְדָרוֹם יְרָשָׁה (דְּבָרִים לג, כג), וּכְתִיב בַּתּוֹרָה: וּרְחָבָה מִנִּי יָם (אִיּוֹב יא, ט)", עַיֵּין שָׁם

. just as is written at the beginning of Sefer HaBahir (section 3): "And from where do we know that the Torah is called 'blessing' (berakhah)? Because it is written: 'And full of the blessing of Hashem, possess the sea (yam) and the south' (Deuteronomy 33:23), and regarding the Torah it is written: 'And broader than the sea (yam)' (Job 11:9)," see there.
וְהַיְינוּ רִיבּוּי בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר "וּרְחָבָה מִנִּי יָם", דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב אוֹתִיּוֹתֶיהָ סְפוּרוֹת וּמְנוּיוֹת

. And this refers specifically to the boundless expansion of the Oral Torah (berakhah from the root bereikhah, a flowing spring), concerning which it is said "and broader than the sea," since the letters of the Written Torah are fixed and counted.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "בְּכָל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ" – בִּרְכַּת ה' הוּא רִיבּוּי בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה

. Thus, the inner meaning of "In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned I will come unto you and bless you" is that the revelation of Hashem's presence ("I will come unto you") brings the blessing of Hashem—the wellspring of the Oral Torah.
וְכֵן כָּאן דִּכְתִיב: "וַיֵּרָא אֵלָי"ו ה'", שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז שֶׁהוֹפִיעַ מִי' חָכְמָה עַל יְדֵי ו' הַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכֹן לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת וְהוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
, And so it is right here in the words "And Hashem appeared
אֵלָיו
(to him)": as we explained above (in Discourse 3), the word
אֵלָיו (אֶל י' ו
') signifies that the supernal light shone from Yud (Chokhmah) through Vav (the middle bar, Tiferet) into the attribute of Malchut, which is the Oral Torah,
וְכֵן כָּל הָאָמוּר בַּפָּרָשָׁה מְרַמֵּז שֶׁזָּכָה לְאוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
, and indeed everything recounted in this parashah alludes to Abraham meriting the light of the Oral Torah,
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר: "עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה שֶׁהֲרֵינִי נִגְלֶה עָלָיו וּמְבָרְכוֹ" – בְּאוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה (הַכָּלוּל בְּתֵיבַת "וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו
"). which is why Rabbi Yitzchak said: "how much more so that I am revealed to him and bless him"—for the very phrase "And He appeared
אֵלָיו
" embodies the blessing of the light of the Oral Torah.

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַיְיתֵי מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְשׁוֹר וָאַיִל לִשְׁלָמִים לִזְבֹּחַ לִפְנֵי ה'" (וַיִּקְרָא ט, ד), וְהַיְינוּ לַמִּדָּה שֶׁ"לִּפְנֵי" שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה (כֶּתֶר, עַתִּיקָא

), And afterward Rabbi Levi brings a second derivation from what is stated: "And an ox and a ram for peace-offerings, to sacrifice before (lifnei) Hashem" (Leviticus 9:4)—where "before Hashem" alludes to the supernal level that precedes the four letters of the Tetragrammaton,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפָרֵשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג עט עַמּוּד ב) הַלָּשׁוֹן "עַל ה'" שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז לְמַזָּלָא קַדִּישָׁא שֶׁהוּא עַתִּיקָא
, just as the holy Zohar (Part III, 79b) explains the phrase "above Hashem (al Hashem)" as referring to Mazala Kadisha (the Holy Constellation), which is Atika (Keter),
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (שָׁם סה עַמּוּד ב) דְּקוֹצָא דְּיוּ"ד דִּלְעֵילָא רְמִיזָא לְאַיִן, כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן, וְהַיְינוּ "עַל ה'" – עַל אוֹתִיּוֹת הֲוָיָ"ה
; based on what is written (there, 65b) that the upper thorn of the Yud alludes to Ayin (Nothingness), Keter Elyon, which stands "above Hashem"—above the four letters of the Tetragrammaton;
וְכֵן מוֹרֶה "לִפְנֵי ה'" עַל מִדַּת עַתִּיקָא שֶׁלִּפְנֵי ה
'. and similarly the phrase "before Hashem (lifnei Hashem)" signifies the level of Atika which precedes the Tetragrammaton.
וְזֶה זוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי "שׁוֹר וָאַיִל" לְאוֹר טַלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא שֶׁמּוֹפִיעַ בְּלֵב הַחֲכָמִים אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁהוּא אוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּגְנַז לַעֲמֵלֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה

. And through the peace-offerings of the "ox and ram" offered "before Hashem," they merited drawing down the supernal dew of Atika (tala de-Atika) which illuminates within the hearts of the sages the light of the Oral Torah—the primordial light of Creation that was hidden away for those who toil in the Oral Torah.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר: "הֲרֵינִי נִגְלֶה עָלָיו וּמְבָרְכוֹ" – רִיבּוּי בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְלָמַד קַל וָחוֹמֶר לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לְאוֹר זֶה עַל יְדֵי הַמִּילָה

. And this is what Rabbi Levi meant by "behold, I am revealed to him and bless him"—bestowing the supernal blessing and abundance of the Oral Torah from Atika—and from this he derived by kal va-chomer that Abraham our father merited this very illumination through the covenant of circumcision.
